notes: No Texas statute requires meal or rest breaks for adults in private employment; federal law does not require them either.
No Texas daily-overtime, minimum-rest-between-shifts, predictive-scheduling, or reporting-time-pay statute; federal weekly overtime applies.
Tex. Lab. Code § 62.0515(a): the state minimum wage supersedes city ordinances governing wages in private employment, so Texas cities have no separate private-sector minimum wage.
Texas 14-15 hour limits (8/day, 48/week) are looser than federal FLSA limits; the resolver keeps the federal limits where stricter.

rules.summary: Texas minimum wage equals the federal minimum wage ($7.25 an hour).

citation.title: Tex. Lab. Code § 62.051 — Minimum wage
citation.excerpt: an employer shall pay to each employee the federal minimum wage under Section 6, Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938

rules.summary: A 14- or 15-year-old enrolled in school may work at most 8 hours a day and 48 a week, and not between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. before a school day (midnight-5 a.m. otherwise).

citation.title: Tex. Lab. Code § 51.013(a)-(b) — Hours of employment (TWC copy of Chapter 51)
citation.excerpt: between the hours of 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. on a day that is followed by a school day; or between the hours of midnight and 5 a.m. on a day that is not followed by a school day

rules.summary: During summer recess a 14- or 15-year-old not in summer school may work at most 8 hours a day and 48 a week, and not between midnight and 5 a.m.

citation.title: Tex. Lab. Code § 51.013(a),(c) — Hours of employment (TWC copy of Chapter 51)
citation.excerpt: is not enrolled in summer school to work between the hours of midnight and 5 a.m. on any day during the time that school is recessed for the summer
